page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.ce4.2xlarge is a memory-optimized virtual machine instance powered by the KVM hypervisor. It features an Intel Xeon 8369HB x86_64 processor with 8 dedicated physical cores and 8 vCPUs running at a clock speed of 3.2 GHz. The instance is equipped with 64.0 GB of RAM, providing a high memory-to-core ratio of 8.0 GB per core. It does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware, and it offers a baseline network bandwidth of 3 Gbps.

Performance benchmarks place this instance primarily in the average tier for general compute tasks. The Intel Xeon processor delivers average single-core and multi-core stress-ng performance, alongside average software compilation and text processing capabilities. However, memory performance shows some divergence; while cached small-block read bandwidth is average at 465.3 GB/sec, uncached large-block read bandwidth and overall PassMark memory scores fall into the bottom 25%. Similarly, database operations and physics simulations show weaker relative performance. Large language model inference on a medium 7B model is poor, though small 135M model inference remains average.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the ecs.ce4.2xlarge provides a high density of memory relative to its compute resources, making it a qualitative fit for workloads requiring substantial RAM without extreme CPU demands. Given the lack of local storage and the moderate network baseline, it is best suited for memory-intensive applications that rely on external storage, such as in-memory caching, Redis deployments, web serving, and lightweight data processing pipelines.
